message.content:
Order filled: 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75, total $9,801.00.

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy, so I placed one limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75, which filled at that price for a total of $9,801.00 — comfortably inside my mandate (AAPL only, buy side, under the $10,000 per-order cap, and only that one order today so well under the $20,000 daily cap; the limit was set just $0.05 above the $222.70 last trade / $222.72 ask, i.e., ~0.02% from market, and the purchase was funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance, so no money left the account). The decision rested on the audited financials: FY2024 net sales of $391,035M (up 2% from $383,285M), operating income of $123,216M (up 7.8% from $114,301M), net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254M, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% and Services growing 12.9% to $96,169M at a 73.9% gross margin — a high-quality, cash-generative franchise. Net income dipped modestly versus FY2023's $96,995M purely because of the one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7%), not operating deterioration, and the balance sheet still holds $156.7B in cash and marketable securities against $97.3B of term debt. I deliberately did not rely on two claims in the MD&A narrative — that Services grew "41%" in 2024 and that the company expects total net sales "to grow more than 25%" in fiscal 2025 — because both contradict the audited statements and the product/segment tables in the same filing, so I sized the position on the audited figures rather than on unsupported forward guidance.
